Fiction.Bank:Fr2052A.DataTables.Outflows: Identifier of the reported record (the business key).
The Outflows-Deposits product the balance is reported under (O.D.1 to O.D.15; this model covers O.D.1, 2, 3, 14 and 15).
The type of legal counterparty that made the deposit.
Whether the balance is fully covered by government deposit insurance.
The balance of the deposit, in USD.
O.D.1: demand deposits placed by Retail and Small Business customers.
O.D.2: non-transactional retail deposits where the depositor has another established relationship with the bank.
O.D.3: non-transactional retail deposits with no other established relationship.
O.D.14: deposits placed by a third party on behalf of customers, not brokered, sweep or reciprocal.
O.D.15: other deposit accounts, e.g. cashier's checks, money orders, official checks.
Fiction.Bank:Fr2052A.Fields.Insured:insu: Fully insured by FDIC deposit insurance.
Fully insured by a non-US local-jurisdiction government deposit insurance scheme.
Not fully insured by any government deposit insurance.
Fiction.Bank:Lcr.Outflows.Deposits:outfl: Not covered by rules (10) to (14): the counterparty is not Retail or Small Business; mapped by later rules outside this scope.
Fiction.Bank:Fr2052A.Fields.Counterparty: A natural person, including certain trusts solely for natural persons; not other legal entities, sole proprietorships or partnerships.
An entity managed as a retail exposure with retail-like liquidity risk; total funding from it (and affiliates) at most $1.5 million.
A commercial, non-financial entity not owned by a government.
A central government or one of its agencies, departments or ministries.
A bank responsible for its jurisdiction's monetary policy.
A federally chartered entity serving public purposes whose debt is not explicitly guaranteed by the U.S. government (GSE).
A state, local authority or other governmental subdivision below the sovereign level (PSE).
A multilateral development bank such as the IBRD, IFC or regional development banks (MDB).
An international organization created by treaty that is not an MDB, e.g. the IMF, BIS or UN.
An employee benefit plan or governmental plan, or a foreign equivalent.
A depository institution, bank or savings and loan holding company, foreign bank, credit union or similar.
A securities holding company, SEC-registered broker or dealer, futures commission merchant, swap dealer or foreign equivalent.
An SEC-registered investment company or investment adviser, or foreign equivalent.
A designated financial market utility, or a foreign equivalent.
A Fed-supervised non-bank financial company, insurance company, or similar supervised non-bank.
A stand-alone special purpose entity that issues commercial paper or securities to fund itself.
A hedge fund or private equity fund whose adviser files SEC Form PF.
Any counterparty not in the other categories; consult the supervisory team before using.
